name: Cetuximab
route_note: IV infusion weekly or every 2 weeks
originator: ImClone Systems (from antibody 225 developed by John Mendelsohn and Gordon Sato)
owner: Eli Lilly (US and Canada); Merck KGaA elsewhere

discovery.by: John Mendelsohn and Gordon Sato (University of California, San Diego)
discovery.note: Murine antibody 225 against EGFR, later made chimeric as C225.

tagline: Chimeric EGFR-blocking antibody for RAS wild-type colorectal and head and neck cancer
summary: Cetuximab is a chimeric IgG1 monoclonal antibody that blocks the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). It is used in RAS wild-type metastatic colorectal cancer and in squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck, including with radiotherapy.
mechanism: Cetuximab binds the extracellular domain III of EGFR with higher affinity than its natural ligands EGF and TGF-α, blocking ligand-induced receptor activation and promoting receptor internalisation and degradation.

This inhibits downstream RAS–RAF–MAPK and PI3K–AKT signalling, reducing proliferation and increasing sensitivity to radiation and chemotherapy; the IgG1 Fc also mediates ADCC. Tumours with activating RAS mutations signal downstream of EGFR and do not respond.
uses: RAS wild-type, EGFR-expressing metastatic colorectal cancer
BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer (with encorafenib)
Locally advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck (with radiotherapy)
Recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma

history.title: Antibody 225
history.detail: Mendelsohn and Sato describe anti-EGFR antibodies that inhibit tumour growth.

history.title: ImClone controversy
history.detail: An FDA refusal-to-file letter in late 2001 and related insider trading lead to the conviction of ImClone's CEO Samuel Waksal in 2002.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved as Erbitux for EGFR-expressing metastatic colorectal cancer.

history.title: Head and neck cancer
history.detail: Approved with radiotherapy for locally advanced head and neck cancer (Bonner trial).

history.title: KRAS selection
history.detail: Labels restrict use to KRAS wild-type colorectal tumours, later extended to all RAS mutations.

history.title: BRAF-mutant colorectal cancer
history.detail: Approved with encorafenib for BRAF V600E-mutant mCRC (BEACON CRC).

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

facts: Severe hypersensitivity reactions are more common in the southern US, linked to pre-existing IgE against galactose-α-1,3-galactose (alpha-gal), associated with tick bites.
Development of acneiform rash correlates with better response.
Benefit is restricted to RAS wild-type colorectal cancers.
